protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: before the fixes, ReadRequestFromClient reads the client-controlled CARD32 Big Request length into unsigned int needed and executes needed <<= 2 before the maxBigRequestSize check. Values above UINT_MAX/4 wrap before the check; the same unchecked conversion occurs again after completing the request header. X.Org's 2025-06-17 advisory describes this exact multiply-before-check overflow, and its 2025-06-18 addendum identifies the second site.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CONFIRMED: git -S, file-addition history, and line history independently converge on ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 as the first surviving write of os/io.c, get_big_req_len, and both needed <<= 2 sites. It is a 609-file R6.6 baseline import, but the authoritative advisory dates the flaw to X11R6.0 and the available older xf-4_0 through xf-4_3 refs contain only hw/ and no recoverable server os/io.c member. Under the protocol, ded6147 is therefore the smallest reconstructable public object, not a later carry, formatting change, or AI-first-selected commit.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED: ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 has the single immediate parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941. That parent resolves, but parent:os/io.c does not exist and parent-wide git grep finds neither get_big_req_len nor needed <<= 2; the vulnerable implementation is absent from the immediate parent. The primary field introducer_parent_absent=false correctly means the parent object itself is available.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: CONFIRMED: ded6147 is a single-parent baseline import, not a merge or a decomposable squash with public member SHAs in this clone. Historical xf-4_0, xf-4_1, xf-4_2, and xf-4_3 branches/tags expose only the hw/ subtree, so no finer X11R6.0 member containing the vulnerable server code can be reconstructed. Leaving squash_decomposed=false and decomposed_shas empty is supported.
